Prior product OPENREP-SUPINTREP-0032 — Assess the military balance in the Taiwan Strait and PRC coercion short of war.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Highly likely that the PRC is conducting a deliberate grey zone coercion campaign to compel Taiwan into political concessions short of war. High-reliability evidence consistently demonstrates coordinated grey zone activities, military modernisation and stated sovereignty claims.

KEY JUDGEMENTS: Highly likely that the PRC is conducting a deliberate grey zone coercion campaign to compel Taiwan into political concessions short of war. High-reliability evidence consistently demonstrates coordinated grey zone activities, military modernisation and stated sovereignty claims.

Unlikely that the PRC military activities near Taiwan are routine training/defence posturing without coercive intent. PRC leaders would prefer to gradually assume control over Taiwan through grey zone coercion and political warfare rather than risk a large-scale conflict that could possibly draw the PRC and the United States—two nuclear powers—into war.

Unlikely that the PRC prioritises dominating the South China Sea (SCS), with Taiwan coercion as a secondary effect. Naval modernisation explicitly targets Taiwan, outweighing an SCS focus.

Realistic possibility that the PRC bases in the SCS, and more generally, PRC domination over or control of its near-seas region could complicate the ability of the United States to intervene militarily in a crisis or conflict between the PRC and Taiwan.

Realistic possibility that the PRC bases in the SCS, and more generally, PRC domination over or control of its near-seas region could help achieve a broader goal of becoming a regional hegemon in its part of Eurasia.

ASSESSMENT: An analysis of competing hypotheses judged that the PRC conducts a deliberate gray zone coercion campaign to compel Taiwan into political concessions short of war. This product assesses that this is highly likely because high-reliability evidence (B-graded) consistently demonstrates coordinated gray zone activities (crs-IF12481), military modernization (crs-RL33153), and stated sovereignty claims (crs-IF12604). No single-source evidence drives this conclusion.

The PRC claims sovereignty over self-ruled Taiwan and has long vowed to unify with it, by force if necessary. PRC leader Xi has declared the PRC will "strive for peaceful reunification," but "will never promise to renounce the use of force" to secure control of Taiwan. To persuade Taiwan and the world to acquiesce to unification, the PRC has stepped up its military activities around Taiwan and sought to isolate Taiwan internationally.

The PRC engages in persistent noncombat operations that erode Taiwan's military and societal resilience. These "gray zone" actions include large-scale military exercises, near-daily patrols around Taiwan that impose operational and maintenance costs on Taiwan's air and naval forces, uncrewed combat aerial vehicle flights encircling Taiwan, cyber operations, stepped-up law enforcement activities near Taiwan-administered islands located just off the PRC coast, and disinformation campaigns and political interference.

Some assess that the PRC uses these activities to sow doubt about Taiwan's military capabilities and to create political pressure for Taipei to acquiesce to Beijing's insistence on unification.
